messages:
Chris B.: hey — noticed a spike in reconnects for a bunch of tenants starting ~09:12 UTC
Ana S.: yup console shows resume_count up 3.8x for that window
Mike P.: are these legit reconnects or hjacked by missed keepalives?
Chris B.: looks like missed keepalives => client reconnects. sse.keepalive.missed metric doubled.
monitor-bot: Alert: sse.keepalive.missed @ p95 increased across prod clusters
Ana S.: recent proxy change added a 200-500ms tail on some requests; our keepalive window is 10s. clients jitter + tail => false positives
Lina R.: if we simply increase server keepalive window we hide real idle drops though — console "active sessions" will look inflated
Mike P.: and billing: every reconnect may create a new session start logged and counted against quota, right?
Chris B.: yep. churn => double-billing in some dashboards; support tickets incoming.
Ana S.: proposal: extend window to 15s server-side, but tag those resumes with metadata so dashboards can filter/credit back if needed
Mike P.: +1 for tagging. also add a sample flag so we don't blow up metrics cardinality. e.g. tag: keepalive_extended=true and keepalive_sample_ratio=0.1
Lina R.: we need rollout UX: console should show which tenants had heuristic applied (canary -> beta -> global) and a checkbox to include/exclude those sessions from "active" counts
Chris B.: quick config snippet I tested locally:
```
# sse keepalive heuristic
sse:
  keepalive_window_ms: 15000
  keepalive_jitter_ms: 4000
  keepalive_extended_tag: "keepalive_extended"
  keepalive_sample_ratio: 0.1
```
Ana S.: looks fine. Can we emit another metric sse.keepalive.extended.count so we can alert if we overuse the heuristic?
Mike P.: yes — also increment a counter with tenant_id hashed for privacy. no PII in metrics.
Lina R.: console change list: 1) add a filter on session lists for keepalive_extended 2) new timeseries for 'extended' vs 'natural' active sessions 3) add note in rollout modal
Chris B.: ops: we should canary in us-east-1 for 6 hours, monitor sse.keepalive.missed, resume_rate, per-tenant billing events. deploy-bot — can you schedule a canary?
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: us-east-1, 6h, config ref sse/keepalive/extend-v1
Ana S.: also add a dashboard panel that shows resume -> new session mapping rate (how many resumes result in billed new session)
Mike P.: if we see increase in 'resume leads to billed start' we rollback immediately. set alert thresholds.
Chris B.: one more flag: server should add `keepalive_reason=proxy_tail` when proxy latency > 300ms so we can debug root cause without changing client code
Lina R.: potential UX snag: product analytics uses active session metric for MAU. we'll need to coordinate with analytics to avoid skewing downstream reports. cc @analytics (we'll ping separately)
Ana S.: ack. I'll draft a short runbook for support: how to identify extended-keepalive cases and file billing disputes.
Chris B.: plan: patch in staging today, canary tomorrow, monitor for 48h, then rollout with console annotations. thumbs if OK
Mike P.: :thumbsup:
Lina R.: :+1:
Ana S.: :shipit:
monitor-bot: Note: added temporary grafana panels for sse.keepalive.extended.count and resume->billed ratio
Chris B.: thanks. filing a short follow-up doc in Confluence after canary completes.
